rawFindings.title: HTTPS proxy targets without an explicit port now ignore the target scheme when config.port is set
rawFindings.explanation: The new `port` expression prefers `config.port` before falling back to the scheme-derived default. For a target like `https://krinkle.dev/w` with `config.port = 9877`, the proxy now connects to port `9877` instead of `443`, even though the target URL is HTTPS and has no explicit port.
rawFindings.suggestion: Preserve the previous precedence: use `proxyDetails.port` if present, otherwise use the scheme default when `proxyDetails.protocol` is set, and only fall back to `config.port` when the target URL has no protocol.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Given `config = {port: 9877, hostname: 'localhost'}` and `proxies = {'/w': 'https://krinkle.dev/w'}`, the created proxy record uses `port: '9877'` and forwards to the wrong upstream port instead of `443`.
